title: HF577 (2023-2024 Regular): Criminal background checks required for firearms transfers, and grounds for disqualification of transferee permit modified.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2023-01-19; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/HF/577/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version (2023-01-19). Strikes the old transferee-permit shortcut around transfer reports, the identity-check rule for unknown parties (subd. 14) and the separate transferee-permit step (subd. 6); the new section 624.7134 replaces them. Exclusions for dealers, family, estates, antiques and temporary range or hunting loans are in 624.7134, subd. 6.

operative_text:
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring possession or ownership of a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): (d) Both the transferor and the transferee must retain a copy of the record of transfer and any attachments to the record of transfer for 20 years from the date of the transfer.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4): (b) A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4): (a) The chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a transferee permit if the applicant is prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon or is determined to be a danger to self or others under paragraph (b). (b) A chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a permit to a person who is a danger to self or others. The decision of the chief of police or sheriff must be based on documented past contact with law enforcement.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 11): A person who makes a false statement in order to obtain a transferee permit knowing or having reason to know the statement is false is guilty of a felony.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 4): No person shall deliver a firearm to a proposed transferee after receiving a written notification that the chief of police or sheriff has determined that the proposed transferee is prohibited by section 624.713 from possessing a firearm.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 8): If the proposed transferee presents a valid permit to carry issued under section 624.714, the transferor need not file a transfer report.
